panels.title: Signup (Railway)
panels.description: External probe of the control plane's /healthz

panels.title: Warden
panels.description: External probe of the provisioner on carrier — also proves Traefik and DNS

panels.title: Landing page
panels.description: External probe of the marketing site

panels.title: carrier metrics
panels.description: Is the box still pushing metrics? DOWN here with probes green means the agent died; DOWN with warden red means the box is gone

panels.title: TLS days left
panels.description: Soonest-expiring cert across all probed endpoints. cert-manager renews at 30 days out; yellow means renewal is late

panels.title: Pods not ready
panels.description: Cluster-wide, completed jobs excluded. Anything nonzero deserves a look

targets.expr: sum(kube_pod_status_ready{condition="false"} unless on(namespace, pod) (kube_pod_status_phase{phase="Succeeded"} == 1)) OR on() vector(0)

panels.title: LLM canary
panels.description: A real claude-opus-5 call through the public gateway path every tenant daemon uses (blackbox bifrost_llm module, every 5m). FAILING = LLM calls are not going through in production and every tenant is running heuristic-only triage - the 2026-08-19 failure mode. NO DATA = the canary itself is not scraping (key unset, blackbox down).

panels.title: CPU busy
panels.description: All 3 shared vCPUs together

panels.title: CPU steal
panels.description: Time a noisy Hetzner neighbor took from our shared vCPUs. Sustained >10% means resize or move

panels.title: Memory used
panels.description: 4 GB total; every tenant daemon eats into this

panels.title: Disk used
panels.description: Root disk full kills the k3s datastore; tenant volume full stops every sync

panels.title: Load average
panels.description: 3 vCPUs, so sustained load above 3 is saturation

panels.title: Network
panels.description: Public interface. Sync bursts are normal; a flat line during business hours is not

panels.title: Container restarts (per hour)
panels.description: Empty is the healthy state — any line here is a crash loop or OOM cycle

panels.title: Memory by pod (top 10)
panels.description: Working set — what the OOM killer judges

panels.title: CPU by pod (top 10)
panels.description: In cores; the node has 3

panels.title: Unhealthy signals
panels.description: Both flat at zero when healthy

targets.expr: sum(kube_pod_status_ready{condition="false"} unless on(namespace, pod) (kube_pod_status_phase{phase="Succeeded"} == 1)) OR on() vector(0)

panels.title: cert-manager: days to expiry
panels.description: passband-wildcard (DNS-01) and warden (HTTP-01). Renewal fires at 30 days; a line sinking below 30 means renewal is failing — check the Cloudflare token first

panels.title: Traefik requests
panels.description: Everything entering the box over 80/443

panels.title: Tenant pods running
panels.description: One pod per tenant. The Google-verification cap is 100

panels.title: Tenant memory
panels.description: Per tenant daemon

panels.title: Tenant CPU
panels.description: Per tenant daemon, in cores

panels.title: Tenant PVC usage
panels.description: Per-tenant mailbox volumes on the shared 50 GB block volume

panels.title: Tenant restarts (per hour)
panels.description: Empty is healthy. A restarting tenant daemon is a tenant not getting mail triaged

panels.title: Image versions live
panels.description: How many distinct daemon image versions the fleet is running right now. 1 is converged, 2 is a roll in flight, 3 or more means a roll stalled partway and nobody noticed.

targets.expr: count(count by (version) (label_replace(kube_pod_container_info{namespace="tenants", container="squelchd"}, "version", "$1", "image_spec", ".*[:@](?:daemon-)?(.+)"))) OR on() vector(0)

panels.title: Off the majority image
panels.description: Pods not yet on whichever image most of the fleet runs. Counts down to 0 as a roll finishes, so a number that stops falling is the roll stalling.

targets.expr: (count(kube_pod_container_info{namespace="tenants", container="squelchd"}) - max(count by (image_spec) (kube_pod_container_info{namespace="tenants", container="squelchd"}))) OR on() vector(0)

panels.title: Image pull failures
panels.description: A wedged roll rather than a slow one: the tag the warden was pointed at does not exist in the registry, or the GHCR pull secret is wrong. Nonzero here means the affected tenants are down, not merely behind.

panels.title: Ahead of the daemon
panels.description: Pods whose spec image is a version the process inside is not reporting: the image rolled but the daemon has not come up on it. Seconds of this per pod is a normal roll; sticky is a crash loop on the new build. Counts only tenants whose daemon exports metrics at all, so it reads 0 rather than lying while squelchd_build_info is still rolling out.

targets.expr: count(max by (tenant, version) (label_replace(label_replace(kube_pod_container_info{namespace="tenants", container="squelchd"}, "version", "$1", "image_spec", ".*[:@](?:daemon-)?(.+)"), "tenant", "$1", "pod", "(.+)-[^-]+-[^-]+")) unless on (tenant, version) squelchd_build_info and on (tenant) squelchd_build_info) OR on() vector(0)

panels.title: Fleet share by version
panels.description: The same roll as a single bar per version. Read it as percent of tenant pods; a roll is done when one bar is at 100%.

panels.title: Pods by image version (what Kubernetes was told to run)
panels.description: The rollout curve, from kube-state-metrics. This moves the instant the warden patches a Deployment, whether or not the new pod ever starts, so it is the honest picture of what has been asked for. Watch the old version's band shrink as the new one grows. The total dips by one at each handoff because a tenant Deployment is Recreate, not RollingUpdate: its SQLite store takes one writer, so the old pod goes away before the new one arrives.

panels.title: Pods by daemon version (what the process reports)
panels.description: The same curve as told from inside the daemons, off port 9464. It lags the panel to its left by however long a pod takes to pull, start and serve. A gap that does not close is a pod that has the new image and cannot run it. Empty for any tenant not yet re-applied with SQUELCH_METRICS_BIND.

panels.title: Version by tenant
panels.description: One band per tenant and version, so the switchover is readable per tenant rather than in aggregate: each band starts when that tenant's pod took that image and ends when it left it. The gap between a tenant's two bands is that tenant's downtime for the release, which Recreate makes unavoidable and which is worth being able to see. A gap that does not close is a pod that never came back.

panels.title: Tenant image inventory
panels.description: The current state as a list: what each tenant was told to run, what its daemon says it is running, and how long that pod has been up (which is how long ago it rolled). Digest is the resolved image ID, the only column that can tell two pulls of the same mutable tag apart.

targets.expr: max by (tenant, pod, version, image_spec, image_id) (label_replace(label_replace(kube_pod_container_info{namespace="tenants", container="squelchd"}, "version", "$1", "image_spec", ".*[:@](?:daemon-)?(.+)"), "tenant", "$1", "pod", "(.+)-[^-]+-[^-]+"))

panels.title: Sync staleness
panels.description: Seconds since that tenant's last successful Gmail sync. The panel this row exists for: a pod can be Running, ready, and completely stuck, and nothing outside the daemon can tell. One line climbing is usually that tenant's Google credential; every line climbing is the box. Alert on 15m.

panels.title: Gmail API errors
panels.description: By kind, per tenant. Empty is healthy. Rate-limit and transient kinds come in bursts and heal themselves; an auth spike does not. A tenant throwing auth errors has a dead refresh token, and no amount of restarting the pod fixes it: that tenant has to re-consent with Google.

panels.title: LLM spend (24h)
panels.description: Rolling 24 hours of stage-2 triage spend, per tenant. The number worth comparing it against is that tenant's configured daily cap; the colours here are a generous default, not the cap.

panels.title: Store on disk
panels.description: The daemon's own view of its SQLite footprint, database and WAL summed. Tenant PVC usage above is the volume's view of the same bytes; the two drifting apart is usually a WAL that stopped checkpointing.

panels.title: Triage throughput
panels.description: Verdicts per second across the fleet, by stage and outcome. Flat at zero while mail is arriving means triage is not running at all. A stage-2 share that climbs means the heuristics stopped catching the easy cases, and the spend panel follows it within the hour.

panels.title: LLM verdict staleness
panels.description: Seconds since that tenant's daemon last got a REAL verdict from any LLM pass (fallbacks and refusals do not count). Grows benignly while no mail arrives, so read it with the LLM canary: canary green + one line climbing = that tenant's key; canary red = the gateway. 0-since-boot renders as huge, which is correct - that daemon's LLM path has never worked. Needs daemon >= 0.0.3.

panels.title: LLM config failures (per hour)
panels.description: Config-level LLM failures per hour by tenant: the gateway rejected the daemon's key, model, or budget (4xx shared by every row). Rows stay queued, so no verdicts are lost - but triage is stalled until the config is fixed. ANY nonzero line is actionable. Needs daemon >= 0.0.3.

list.name: New daemon image
list.expr: count by (version) (label_replace(kube_pod_container_info{namespace="tenants", container="squelchd"}, "version", "$1", "image_spec", ".*[:@](?:daemon-)?(.+)")) unless count by (version) (label_replace(kube_pod_container_info{namespace="tenants", container="squelchd"} offset 10m, "version", "$1", "image_spec", ".*[:@](?:daemon-)?(.+)"))
